text: Paper and book atlas / 2001 Interaction of Small Planar Perturbations with Cooling-Conductive Fronts Shchekinov & Ibáñez · 2001 ApJ 563, 209–220 Reference listed · scope proposed Acoustic and entropy perturbations interact with steady subsonic cold–hot fronts in one-dimensional planar geometry, with heating, cooling, and thermal conduction. Scope in this archive. First audit the steady planar background and its mass-flux eigenvalue at prescribed pressure, as discussed by Iwasaki & Inutsuka (2012), section 3. Then consider reflection/transmission coefficients as a separate perturbation benchmark. Do not equate this one-dimensional perturbation problem with transverse front corrugation. Source review: Bibliography and author-uploaded abstract checked; the mass-flux eigenvalue connection was checked in Iwasaki & Inutsuka (2012), section 3. Original equations and target figures still require a dedicated audit. Source notes and related resources. Planar fronts & steady flow → Original publication and bibliography.
